propositions: The substring-based CI ChatOps matcher in gerrit_to_platform.ini.template maps 'recheck' to verify workflow, and the old LLM retrigger word 'recheck-review' embedded this substring, causing CI runs to be cancelled when the bot's own replies re-triggered the matcher.
The new trigger token 'rerun-llm-review' shares no substring in either direction with any [mapping comment-added] key from the ini template, preventing future collisions.

All bot-posted replies (_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE, _refusal_message, and the new retired-word refusal) must be scrubbed of any ini-mapped trigger words to prevent the bot's own comments from re-dispatching CI.
Comments containing the retired word 'recheck-review' now post exactly one refusal reply naming the new trigger and enqueue no review event or label write.
The handler places the retired-word refusal after the project guard and change re-anchoring to ensure post_comment never replies on out-of-project changes.
Test assertions parse the ini template at runtime to enforce substring-disjointness and bot-reply scrubbing, so future colliding CI mappings fail in tests rather than production.
